newsitem.title: BULGARIA: PRESS DIGEST - BULGARIAN BUSINESS WEEKLIES -MAY 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - BULGARIAN BUSINESS WEEKLIES -MAY 26.

text.p: The following stories were reported in this week's Bulgarian business weeklies. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

-- Bulgaria Insurance Holding, one of the country's biggest insurance groupings, has sent a proposal to the central bank to buy the ailing private Yambol bank, which has been in receivership since September 1996.
The holding said it was ready to invest some three billion levs to raise the bank's capital from 17 million levs and to cover the bank's debts.
-- The Sofia City Court postponed ruling on an insolvency case against state-owned Economic Bank, in receivership since September, for July 8.

-- The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) board approved subsciption to 20 percent of newly issued shares of Bulgaria's First Investment Bank capital at an aggregate subscription price not exceeding 5.2 million European Currency Units ($6 million), the EBRD said.
The EBRD also said it expected to finalise a deal to buy a 35 percent stake in the state-owned United Bulgarian Bank by early July.
-- Switzerland's Surito Investments said it was ready to invest some $25 million in Bulgaria's First Private Bank (FPB) if the Bulgarian National Bank restored its licence.
On May 15 the BNB revoked the FPB licence, citing failure to collect extended credits during the one-year period of receivership, which expired on May 16.
-- Bulgaria will restructure its central bank in line with pledges to the International Monetary Fund to introduce a restrictive fixed exchange rate regime, called a currency board system.
Bulgaria's parliament was expected to appoint the head of the currency board together with approving a new Bulgarian National Bank Act, prime minister Ivan Kostov said.

-- Bulgaria's state carrier Balkan Airlines financial consultant KPMG advised on a scheme to clear some $37 million of Balkan debts to banks. Under the scheme the state should restructure Balkan debts to four local commercial banks against debts of those banks to the Finance ministry.
-- The new Bulgarian cabinet took office on Wednesday and said its priorities were speeding up reforms, cracking down on organised crime and bringing Bulgaria into the European Union and NATO.

-- Bulgaria's parliament is expected to appoint a new chairman of the State Savings Bank, the country's largest savings institution after current chairman Bistra Dimitrova said on May 21 she would resign.
